text.p: Following are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The caretaker government is planning to hold national census in the first fortnight of January, sources said.
- The caretaker Punjab governor dismissed the provincial cabinet, dissolved the assembly on multiple charges and appointed Mian Afzal Hayat as caretaker chief minister.
- Caretaker Prime Minister Meraj Khalid reiterated his government's commitment to hold general elections on February 3 and said members of his cabinet were barred from standing.
- Jemima Khan, wife of former Pakistani cricket captain Imran Khan, gave birth to a baby boy.

- Deposed Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto demanded restoration of her government, saying she would be ready to work out modalities with the opposition for forming a caretaker administration until elections were held.
- Banks will now earn 17 percent annual return on the rupee equivalent of foreign currency deposits they bring in by December 10 instead of the previous deadline of November 28, bankers said.
- The caretaker government is seriously considering allowing free trade with India, Commerce Ministry sources said.
- The United States has agreed to lift a 45-day-old ban on import of Pakistani shrimps within a week, Pakistan Seafood Industries Association said.
- The caretaker government has asked provincial governments to start assessment of wealth tax on agricultural assets.
- Former federal minister for science and technology Nawaz Khokhar was arrested at a hotel in Lahore.
- The government is considering abolishing pre-shipment inspection of goods for import and export, sources said.
- Foreign banks are demanding better pricing for bringing in foreign currency deposits from abroad since overseas investors are demanding a higher country risk fee, sources said.
- The government is likely to establish a Foreign Investment Advisory Board to attract foreign investors..
